items.description: Geometry Foundation Models (GFMs) have substantially advanced monocular 3D reconstruction, yet extending this capability to 4D dynamic understanding remains a fundamental challenge. Most existing motion perception methods (e.g., sparse tracking, dense point-wise flow) treat motion as independent point-wise displacements, ignoring the structured nature of physical motion. items.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
items.description: LLM training is shifting from manual design and annotation to interaction-driven self-evolution. items.title: Explainable Reinforcement Learning for assisting Air Traffic Controllers
items.description: To effectively integrate AI into high-stakes, critical environments such as healthcare, autonomous driving, and aviation--and to advance toward higher levels of automation and seamless human-AI collaboration--building trust in AI-driven solutions is essential. items.description: Adding procedural skills to an LLM agent is typically evaluated by average improvement in task success. However, this metric hides an important cost: skills can also make agents worse. We measure both sides by comparing agents with and without skills across nearly 6,000 runs spanning two office automation benchmarks and three model harness stacks. items.title: Opaque Epistemic Mediation: How LLM Deployment Configurations Shape the Validation of Pseudo-Science

items.title: CausalForge: A Formally Grounded, Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Automated Research in Causal Inference
items.description: Automating theoretical research is constrained not only by the generation of candidate results, but also by their reliable evaluation. A common approach is to close the research loop with a large language model (LLM) reviewer. items.title: Interpretable EEG biomarkers with bag-of-waves: Spatial and temporal waveform dictionaries for low-data regimes
items.description: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used to diagnose neurological conditions, but its analysis usually relies on either predefined spectral features or deep neural networks. items.title: Susceptible Reservoir Architectures for Regime-Conditional Volatility Forecasting

items.title: \k{appa}-LoRA: Condition Numbers Reveal Which LoRA Matrices Worth Updating
items.description: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely adopted technique for efficient neural network fine-tuning, decomposing model updates into low-rank matrices. items.title: Complexity Bounds and Approaches to Learning Projected Gradient Descent Solver Iterates
items.description: Data scarcity poses a fundamental challenge in training generative models to produce initial guesses for parametric optimization problems that are otherwise numerically expensive to solve. items.title: TRACE-ROUTER: Task-Consistent and Adaptive Online Routing for Agentic AI
items.description: Routing to select large language models (LLMs) with different cost-quality trade-offs has become a fundamental deployment feature of enterprise AI. However, agentic applications execute as long-horizon workflows whose quality is determined only by a delayed, task-level outcome. items.description: Generative AI is reshaping programming education, yet educators often infer students' AI-supported learning from classroom observations alone. items.title: grapheme-kit: Grapheme-Level Metrics and Text Processing for Multilingual NLP
items.description: Existing lexical distance, similarity, and evaluation metrics operate on Unicode code points, which can misrepresent errors in writing systems where a single grapheme is represented by multiple Unicode code points. We introduce grapheme-kit, an open-source Python library that extends these metrics to operate on grapheme clusters instead. items.name: Dynamic Capability Scoping for Enterprise AI Agents: A Synthetic Dataset and Three-Source Permission Architecture
items.title: Dynamic Capability Scoping for Enterprise AI Agents: A Synthetic Dataset and Three-Source Permission Architecture
items.description: Enterprise AI agents are typically granted static credential sets at configuration time, holding every tool the role might need for every task they perform. This persistent over-privilege expands the attack surface. We argue that capability scoping must follow a dynamic least-privilege principle and be treated as a prevention mechanism before a detection one. items.title: Reflector: Arrangement-Aware Harmonic Retrieval for Sample-Based Composition
items.description: Sample retrieval tools can help composers find harmonically compatible material, but querying from a fixed reference sample becomes less informative as arrangements evolve and the harmonic context shifts with each musical decision.
